hypothesis: The exit-guard watchdog's FORCE_QUIT_AFTER_MS=1500 deadline (armed at the second Ctrl+C or the exit decision) fires mid-flush on a terminal that drains the exit flush slower than the deadline: the flush is the frozen scrollback contract (8.74MB at 32,286 rows) and a slow consumer (~0.5-2MB/s, the pyte/laggy-ssh class) makes it outlast the deadline, so the watchdog force-quits a HEALTHY drain - printing 'shutdown stalled; forced exit.' (a port-only message; TS has no watchdog and simply waits for its writes), killing the process with 64-82% of the flush unwritten (truncated scrollback), and queueing the restore bytes mid-stream. A drain-aware guard - the writer reports progress per completed flush chunk, the release tail and the resume hint report theirs, and the watchdog holds its fire while progress landed within a grace window - keeps the hard 1500ms ceiling for the genuinely-stalled/wedged case while letting a healthy slow drain finish byte-identically.

TS parity first: TS tui.ts/interactive-mode.ts verified - NO watchdog, NO forced exit, NO stall message (handleCtrlC 2nd press = async shutdown; slow writes just wait; EXIT_HINT_DURATION_MS=2000 only gates the hint). CANDIDATE (lane/hillclimb-slow-drain-exitguard, base 9b62f26af, folded e6e7a26e4): exit_guard.rs gains EXIT_PROGRESS_GRACE_MS=500 + a process-global progress stamp (Mutex<Option<Instant>>) fed by pub note_exit_progress(); the watchdog's fire condition becomes force_quit_due(deadline passed AND progress stale > grace); spawn_watchdog holds per 25ms poll slice; view.rs CHUNK_BYTES 256KiB->32KiB (a completed 32KiB chunk lands within the 500ms grace for any drain >= ~65KB/s) + feeds after every chunk write (FlushSink::feed chunk boundary, finish append-tail, finish repaint); exit_restore.rs terminal_release_tail feeds after the cursor-show execute and the final flush; pa-cli interactive_mode.rs print_resume_hint feeds after the hint print (the composition root's 300ms pre-exit delay sits inside the grace of the fresh stamp). New real-pty e2e (pa-cli slow_drain_exit_guard_e2e.rs, the kitty-release harness pattern: the test binary re-executes itself in child mode against a mock supervisor over a pty with setsid+TIOCSCTTY, paced master reads at 96KB/s): the slow leg asserts the whole transcript flushes with no forced exit and the restore tail lands last; the stalled leg (2.5s dead consumer mid-flush) asserts the fire structurally (the forced restore's second alt-screen leave + the flush cut + exit 0). parity_notes: TS-FIRST: TS has NO exit-guard watchdog at all (packages/tui/src/tui.ts + coding-agent interactive-mode.ts: handleCtrlC's second press runs the async shutdown(); there is no forced exit and no 'shutdown stalled' string anywhere in the TS tree) - the port's watchdog is documented hardening for the wedged-loop case (issue #138). On a HEALTHY slow drain TS simply waits for its writes; the candidate restores exactly that (hold on observed progress) while keeping the port's hardening: the 1500ms ceiling still fires with no progress for a grace window (the wedged loop - the case the guard was built for), and a stalled drain (dead consumer) fires with the same message and exit code 0. The user-visible 'Prime Agent: shutdown stalled; forced exit.' line and its trigger semantics are unchanged text and unchanged for the genuine-stall case; it no longer prints on a healthy drain. The flushed byte stream is the frozen scrollback contract: IDENTICAL base-vs-cand on every non-fired leg (40k/10k/2k raw + 2k pyte, shas e284469e/b690d465/e3d55950) and IDENTICAL across drain rates on the candidate (the slow legs' flush sha == the raw legs' flush sha); the tmux real-terminal scrollback at 10k is 1863/1864 lines byte-identical across arms (the only differing line is tmux's own dead-pane timestamp). The exit tail still restores the terminal (tail_after_flush on every non-fired leg; the e2e asserts the restore follows the last flushed row). Disclosed floor: with 32KiB chunks + 500ms grace, drains slower than ~65KB/s read as stalled and force-quit (deliberate: the port's 1500ms contract outranks an unbounded wait; TS would wait indefinitely - the ceiling is the operational escape hatch for the wedged case, same class as the PRIME_AGENT_TUI_EXIT_FLUSH kill-switch ruling). Disclosed: a stalled drain that fires still truncates the flush (the fire is committed at decision time; the restore writes queue behind the writer's blocked chunk on the stdout lock - strace-proven). baseline_decompose_9b62f26af.strace_mechanism: the watchdog's restore writes WIN the PTY FIFO race at a flush-chunk boundary (the writer is in its encode gap when space frees): force_quit's ~21B restore + 44B message land mid-stream, exit_group(0) kills the process while the writer holds the remaining chunks unwritten. SECOND mechanism: force_quit's writes contend on std::io::stdout()'s process-global lock - the main thread's blocked chunk write HOLDS it, so the watchdog's restore waits for the lock (observed 1.22s futex wait in the e2e stall leg) and lands only when the writer's current write returns. The pre-#2913 single-write flush 'held priority' (the watchdog starved until the whole flush drained, no truncation in 3/3); the chunked flush loses that accidental protection
baseline_decompose_9b62f26af.watchdog_fire_windows: fired legs exit at press2+1586..1671ms (the 1500ms deadline + arm/jitter); stall legs (consumer dead 2.5s): fire during the stall, restore+message queue behind the full FIFO, exit observed right after the drain resumes
